headline: Clorox drops as ERP lap and GOJO step-up compress margins
summary_short: Clorox's Q4 FY2026 net sales fell 2% to $1.95B (organic -13%) as the year-ago ERP-transition shipment lap distorted the comparison, while the April-closed GOJO acquisition added ~10 points to reported sales. Adjusted EPS dropped 42% to $1.66; the company issued initial FY2027 diluted EPS guidance of $5.41-$5.71.
summary_long: Reported net sales of $1.95B included ~10 points from the GOJO/Purell acquisition. Organic sales fell 13%, with ~13.5 points attributable to lapping incremental ERP-transition shipments in Q4 FY2025. Gross margin compressed 520 bps to 41.3% on lower volume, GOJO inventory step-up (~150 bps), commodity costs, and manufacturing/logistics costs, partially offset by cost savings. GAAP EPS $1.34 (-50% y/y) included GOJO transaction/integration costs; adjusted EPS $1.66 (-42%). Segment: Health & Wellness sales +16% but adjusted EBIT -15%; Household -18%/-56% EBIT; Lifestyle -17%/-60% EBIT; International +4%/+17% EBIT. FY2026 net sales $6.72B (-5%); operating cash flow $612M (-38%) on the Glad Venture termination payment. FY2027 outlook: net sales +13-14%, organic +3.5-4.5%, GAAP EPS $5.41-$5.71, adjusted EPS $5.70-$6.00.

drivers.explanation: Lapping the ~13.5 percentage points of incremental ERP-transition shipments in the year-ago quarter; GOJO acquisition added about 10 points offset.
Lower volume, GOJO inventory step-up (~150 bps), higher commodity costs, and higher manufacturing and logistics costs, partially offset by cost savings.
Lower net sales and gross margin combined with GOJO transaction-related costs including inventory step-up and integration costs, partially offset by lapping prior-year digital investments.
Primarily driven by the Glad Venture Agreement termination payment.

Management called results in line with expectations and framed FY2027 as still challenging (cost volatility, value-seeking consumer) but starting from a stronger position after completing the ERP transition and GOJO integration.
